gap_follow_direct_after_algorithm_change.note: gap_switch_margin (hysteresis) + corner_speed 0.8->1.1 + corner_speed_wide, cornering anticipation left off (see gap_follow's README, 'Three additions from a real-hallway report'). Wall contact -6%, speed +2% -- this course is uniformly narrow (1.5m corridor, 1.2m corner radius near the car's own turning-circle floor), so the improvement is modest and geometry-limited, consistent with docs/ros-simulator.md's asb_10000 section. None of the weave-fix's actual value (does the car look less 'drunk') is measurable from this aggregate distance/contact metric -- that needs a real low-speed run to judge.

gap_follow_direct_indoor_wide_before_and.note: Clean win on the wide course: +10% average speed, wall contact still zero both ways. Driven almost entirely by corner_speed_wide/corner_speed, since the margin never shrinks on a corridor this wide (width_factor stays at 1.0) and cornering anticipation is off. An earlier run with cornering anticipation left ON measured a ~25% average-speed *regression* here (1.43m/s) for no matching safety benefit -- see gap_follow's README for why, and why it now ships disabled.
